Maya — thanks for the clear ask. Quick take up front, then a short appendix attached.

Recommendation A (Conservative): Stay on Compact + purchase a 30% throughput credit buffer.
- Pros: lower baseline cost, avoid a full tier uplift; credits cover bursty periods.
- Cons: potential higher tail latency on sustained load; may hit pacing limits.
- Downgrade path: unused credits roll forward for one quarter; option to auto-upgrade to Core if 7-day average QPS > 2x baseline for 14 days.

Recommendation B (Predictable SLOs): Move to Core tier with bundled advanced observability and canary rollouts.
- Pros: predictable latency SLO, built-in rollout and A/B tooling, easier procurement (single line item).
- Cons: higher committed spend; less granular seat/throughput trade.

Attached: packaging-options.xlsx (decision matrix + sample quote). Also threw in a one-page summary you can share with procurement.

If this looks right I can loop Ben for concession options and Kimberly for the technical sizing notes. When is a good time Monday to sync?

— Priyom

Looping in sizing guidance for transparency:

- Observed profile from your usage file: 65% short requests (<128 tokens), 20% mid (128-512), 15% long (>512). That distribution favors Compact with aggressive prefix caching and KV reuse.
- If you rely heavily on streaming + reranking concurrently, tail latency risk increases under Compact during sustained bursts — Core gives headroom and better default batching.
- Quantized model variants can reduce token cost ~20% but may slightly affect rare-case hallucination sensitivity; suggest running the pilot with quantized Core variant behind a canary route.

Action: Priyom, I prepared a simple token-distribution sheet that maps expected monthly spend under both recommendations. Attaching now.
